title: Number of Effective Subsequences
summary: Given an integer array, calculate the number of subsequences whose removal strictly decreases the bitwise OR of the remaining elements, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an integer array, calculate the number of subsequences whose removal strictly decreases the bitwise OR of the remaining elements, modulo 10^9 + 7. The bitwise OR of an empty array is 0.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 positive integers below 2^20.
A removed nonempty subsequence is effective when the OR of remaining indices is strictly below the original OR.
reference_solution:
def count_effective_or_removals(nums):
    mod=10**9+7;full=0
    for value in nums:full|=value
    bits=max(1,full.bit_length());size=1<<bits;frequencies=[0]*size
    for value in nums:frequencies[value]+=1
    subset_counts=frequencies[:]
    for bit in range(bits):
        step=1<<bit
        for mask in range(size):
            if mask&step:subset_counts[mask]+=subset_counts[mask^step]
    powers=[1]*(len(nums)+1)
    for index in range(len(nums)):powers[index+1]=powers[index]*2%mod
    answer=0;chosen=full
    while chosen:
        disjoint=subset_counts[(size-1)^chosen];term=powers[disjoint]
        if chosen.bit_count()%2:answer+=term
        else:answer-=term
        chosen=(chosen-1)&full
    return answer%mod

hints: The remaining OR drops exactly when at least one original bit loses every element carrying it.
For a chosen nonempty bit subset, all elements intersecting it must be removed, while disjoint elements are optional.
Use SOS subset sums to count disjoint elements for every bit subset, then inclusion–exclude over subsets of the original OR.
Each event is one cleared bit; their intersections have 2^(optional disjoint elements) removals, so inclusion–exclusion counts their union exactly.

tests.explanation: Removing all carriers of bit zero or bit one gives three distinct effective subsequences.
Only removing both copies clears the sole present bit, giving one.
